title: Natural Domain of a Rational Function with Quadratic Denominator
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain of the rational function g(x) = \frac{3x + 1}{x^2 - 9}. Express the domain as a union of open intervals.
hints: Identify any values of x that would cause division by zero in the denominator.
Factor the quadratic denominator x^2 - 9 as a difference of two squares.
Remove the real roots of the denominator from the real number line.

steps.title: Formulate Denominator Singularity Condition
steps.explanation: A rational function is undefined precisely where its denominator equals zero.
steps.why: Division by zero is undefined in arithmetic and calculus.

steps.title: Factor the Denominator
steps.explanation: Factoring the difference of squares reveals two distinct real roots, x = 3 and x = -3, which must be excluded from the domain.
steps.why: The product of two real numbers is zero if and only if at least one factor is zero.

steps.title: Express the Domain in Interval Notation
steps.explanation: Removing -3 and 3 from the real line partitions R into three open sub-intervals.
steps.why: Removing two isolated points from the real number line creates the union of three disjoint open intervals.
